options.text: The ovaries
The uterus
The cervix
The fallopian tubes

questions.explanation: Egg cells (ova) are produced in the ovaries. A woman is born with all her egg cells already present. Each month from puberty, one egg matures and is released during ovulation.

questions.stem: What is the function of the fallopian tube (oviduct)?

options.text: To produce hormones that control the menstrual cycle
To store eggs until they are needed
To carry the egg from the ovary to the uterus and is where fertilisation occurs
To protect the developing embryo

questions.explanation: The fallopian tube (oviduct) carries the egg from the ovary towards the uterus. Fertilisation normally occurs in the fallopian tube. Cilia and muscular contractions help move the egg along.

questions.stem: What is the role of the uterus (womb)?

options.text: To produce egg cells
To provide a place for the embryo to implant and develop during pregnancy
To release hormones into the blood
To filter waste from the blood

questions.explanation: The uterus is a muscular organ where the fertilised egg implants into the thick lining and develops during pregnancy. The uterus lining provides nutrients and protection for the developing embryo and fetus.

options.text: The muscle that pushes the baby out during birth
The outer part of the female reproductive system
The opening between the vagina and the uterus
The tube connecting the ovary to the uterus

questions.explanation: The cervix is the narrow opening at the lower end of the uterus that connects it to the vagina. It remains tightly closed during pregnancy to protect the developing fetus and dilates during labour to allow the baby to pass through.

questions.stem: How is an egg cell adapted for its function?

options.text: It has a thick cell wall for protection from enzymes
It has many mitochondria and moves very quickly
It is large with a food reserve (cytoplasm) and a protective jelly layer
It has a tail for swimming and is very small

questions.explanation: The egg cell is much larger than a sperm cell and contains a large amount of cytoplasm as a food reserve for the early embryo. It has a protective jelly layer (zona pellucida) that changes after fertilisation to prevent other sperm entering.

questions.stem: Which two hormones are produced by the ovaries?

options.text: Oestrogen and progesterone
FSH and LH
Adrenaline and thyroxine
Insulin and glucagon

questions.explanation: The ovaries produce oestrogen (which repairs the uterus lining and triggers LH release) and progesterone (which maintains the uterus lining). These hormones play essential roles in the menstrual cycle and pregnancy.

questions.stem: How does the egg move along the fallopian tube?

options.text: Gravity pulls it downward towards the uterus
It swims using a tail like a sperm cell
Cilia lining the tube waft it along, aided by muscular contractions
Blood flow pushes it through the tube

questions.explanation: The egg cannot move on its own. It is swept along the fallopian tube by tiny hair-like cilia that line the tube, combined with gentle peristaltic (muscular) contractions of the tube wall.
